lead.headline: Deadly Strike Hits Riyadh's Main Airport
lead.deck: Saudi authorities say an attack on the capital's international airport killed 12 people and wounded more than 300, raising fears that a regional conflict could spread further.
body: An airport is usually where people leave one country and arrive in another. On Saturday, King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia's capital, was evacuated after a missile strike. Saudi authorities said 12 people were killed and more than 300 wounded.

The attack is part of a wider conflict involving Saudi Arabia, Yemen's Houthi movement and Iran. The Houthis have claimed attacks on Saudi infrastructure and say they are retaliating for Saudi actions. Saudi Arabia and its partners blame the Houthis, who receive support from Iran. Claims about responsibility should be checked carefully.

Riyadh's airport connects Saudi Arabia to the world, carrying families, religious visitors, business travellers and cargo. An attack can disrupt flights and force governments to weigh civilian protection against the risk of widening the conflict.

map.title: THE SOUTHERN GULF REGION
map.footnote: Schematic regional locator; not to scale
map.caption: Saudi Arabia borders Yemen to the south; the conflict's effects can travel far beyond the battlefield.

lead.why: One attack can trigger retaliation, which can trigger another response. Saudi Arabia may seek help from allies, while the United States must weigh deterrence against deeper involvement. The region also sits near important shipping and energy routes, so insecurity can affect fuel prices far away. The next question is whether leaders widen the conflict or make room for diplomacy.

p1_stories.headline: Panama Faces a Long Aftershock Watch
p1_stories.deck: A powerful earthquake and continuing aftershocks have sent residents outdoors, damaged infrastructure and prompted emergency measures.
body: A powerful earthquake shook Panama on Friday, sending people into streets and open spaces. Reports described a magnitude of 7.7, followed by aftershocks and damage in several communities. Authorities urged caution near damaged buildings and coastal areas.

Earthquakes occur when stress along a fault is suddenly released. Magnitude describes the size of a quake at its source; each whole-number increase represents a large jump in energy. Aftershocks follow as the crust adjusts and can still be dangerous.

Panama is a narrow bridge between North and South America and home to the Panama Canal, a shipping shortcut between the Atlantic and Pacific. The canal was reported operational in initial coverage, while crews assessed roads, utilities and buildings.

illustration.title: AFTER THE SHAKING
illustration.subtitle: Panama • Oct. 2026
illustration.caption: Aftershocks can continue after the main earthquake; damaged structures need careful inspection.

p1_stories.connect: Preparedness matters before the ground moves. Building codes, emergency alerts, evacuation routes and drills can reduce harm even when a quake cannot be predicted precisely. The canal is globally important, but people nearby depend on local roads, power, hospitals and rescue workers.

p2_stories.headline: Delhi Tightens Security Before Youth Protest
p2_stories.deck: Police detained more than 2,000 people and restricted parts of the capital ahead of a rally demanding answers about voter-list changes.
body: Parts of New Delhi faced heavy security on Saturday as authorities stopped a rally led by the youth group known as the Cockroach movement. Reuters reported more than 2,000 detentions and disruptions to some internet services and metro stations.

The protest concerns revisions to voter lists overseen by India's Election Commission. Critics say the changes removed many names and could unfairly affect opposition voters; election authorities and the government reject allegations of wrongdoing.

Voter lists determine who can cast a ballot. In a large country, keeping them accurate is difficult as people move or turn 18. The key test is whether the process is transparent and eligible voters can challenge mistakes.
p2_stories.why: Democracy depends on more than holding elections. People need confidence that rules are fair, eligible voters can participate and complaints are reviewed independently. Authorities must keep gatherings safe, while people have rights to peaceful assembly. Evidence and a credible process matter more than slogans.
also: India's central bank raised its key policy rate to 5.5% on Oct. 7, its first increase in nearly four years, as inflation pressures grew.
Higher energy prices can raise transport and manufacturing costs, eventually affecting household budgets.

p2_stories.headline: Storm Damage Leaves Communities Without Power
p2_stories.deck: Hurricane Isaias made landfall in Florida as a Category 2 storm before weakening, while heavy rain and wind continued to threaten parts of the Southeast.
body: Hurricane Isaias came ashore near Destin, Florida, as a Category 2 storm, AP reported. Heavy rain, fallen trees and power outages continued across parts of the Southeast; early coverage reported at least four deaths.

A hurricane category measures sustained wind, not every danger. Rain can flood roads, trees can fall, and generators used indoors can cause deadly carbon-monoxide poisoning. Follow local warnings even after a storm weakens.

chart.title: HURRICANE CATEGORY SCALE
chart.subtitle: Saffir-Simpson wind categories (1–5)
chart.caption: Category measures sustained wind only; rainfall and storm surge can also be dangerous. Category 4 is shown for comparison, not as Isaias's category.

p2_stories.why: Storms become disasters when hazards meet vulnerable people and infrastructure. Strong building standards, reliable alerts and evacuation plans reduce risk. Climate trends require decades of data; one storm alone cannot prove a long-term pattern.
p2_stories.analyst: Think like an analyst: a storm category measures wind, but risk also depends on flooding, housing and power access. What local facts would you check before deciding a neighbourhood is safe?

briefs: Panama: Residents and officials are assessing damage and monitoring aftershocks after Friday's powerful earthquake.
Sudan: An AP report says a drone strike near the Ethiopian border killed dozens of people.

vocab.def: A situation becoming more intense or dangerous. Today: responses to the Riyadh attack could widen or contain the conflict.
A smaller quake following a larger one. Today: Panama is watching for more shaking.
The official list of people eligible to vote. Today: India is debating changes to voter lists.
Essential systems such as roads, power lines and airports. Today: storms and attacks can disrupt them.

learn.did_you_know: The Panama Canal links the Atlantic and Pacific. Its locks raise and lower ships to Gatun Lake, so vessels can cross Central America instead of sailing around South America.
learn.quote: A useful question in a crisis is not only 'What happened?' but also 'What do we know, and how do we know it?'

sports.title: Cricket: New Zealand lose a key fast bowler
sports.body: New Zealand fast bowler Will O'Rourke will miss the India series while recovering from injuries, Reuters reported. The tour begins October 22.
